cards.name: Switch Selection Tools
cards.path: Edit/Keyboard Shortcuts.../Menu Commands/Other Select/Switch Selection Tools
cards.summary: Keyboard-only command (no visible menu item) that swaps the active tool between Illustrator's selection tools; presumably the Selection Tool and the Direct Selection Tool, but which tools it cycles has not been confirmed. It changes nothing in the artwork, only the tool in hand.
use_for: flipping between moving whole objects and editing their anchor points while refining a logo
fast path editing on icons without a trip to the toolbar
avoid: picking one specific tool: press V for the Selection Tool or A for the Direct Selection Tool instead of toggling
scripts that need a known tool: pick it explicitly with app.selectTool instead of toggling
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("switchSelTool") (command string paired from Defaults.kys, not confirmed by execution); to set a known tool: app.selectTool("Adobe Select Tool") or app.selectTool("Adobe Direct Select Tool") (tool ids from the ai_tool harvest; unverified)

review.changes: summary no longer claims the name says which tools it toggles; replaced the unharvested hold-Ctrl claim with the harvested V / A tool shortcuts; app.selectTool now names real ai_tool ids

cards.name: Bold
cards.summary: Text-editing shortcut that makes the selected characters bold, presumably by switching them to the Bold style of their font family (Illustrator has no faux bold in the Character panel). What happens when the family has no Bold style is unverified. Works only while the cursor is in text.
use_for: emphasising a word inside a body-copy paragraph on a flyer
bolding a price or key figure in a product label without opening the font menu
avoid: a family without a Bold style: choose a heavier weight from the font-style menu instead
styling many headings consistently: use a character style, not per-word shortcuts
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("~textBold") (inferred id, text-editing context, likely needs a live text selection). Dependable DOM route: set textRange.characterAttributes.textFont to the app.textFonts item whose .family is the current font's family and whose .style is its Bold style (unverified)

review.changes: DOM route no longer guesses a "<Family>-Bold" font name (getByName takes the full font name); it now picks the Bold style via TextFont.family / .style

cards.name: Center Text
cards.summary: Sets the paragraph alignment of the selected text (or of every paragraph in selected type objects) to Align Center, so each line is centred on the type object's anchor or area width. Same result as the Align Center button in the Paragraph panel.
use_for: centred poster headlines and event titles
invitation and certificate copy
badge and logo lockup text
avoid: long body text: ragged both sides is hard to read, use Left Align Text
centring the text object on the page: that is Align panel / Horizontal Align Center, not paragraph alignment
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("centerAlign") (inferred id); DOM: textRange.paragraphAttributes.justification = Justification.CENTER (unverified)

review.changes: none

cards.name: Clear Tracking
cards.summary: Resets tracking on the selected text to 0, undoing any letter-spacing added or removed; Adobe's shortcut list describes it as resetting tracking/kerning to 0, so manual kerning may be cleared too (unconfirmed). Letter-spacing goes back to what the kerning setting alone produces.
use_for: cleaning up a headline that was over-tracked before re-spacing it
normalising text pasted from another file with odd letter-spacing
avoid: text where deliberate wide tracking is part of the design (spaced caps logotypes): it removes it
fixing one awkward pair only: adjust kerning at that pair instead
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("clearTrack") (inferred id); DOM: textRange.characterAttributes.tracking = 0 (unverified)

review.changes: summary no longer claims spacing returns to the font's built-in metrics (kerning may survive the reset)

cards.name: Font Size Step Down
cards.path: Edit/Keyboard Shortcuts.../Menu Commands/Other Text/Font Size Step Down
cards.summary: Shrinks the selected type by a bigger step than Point Size Down; Adobe's shortcut docs describe it as a multiple of the Size/Leading increment in Preferences > Type, but the step size is not in this harvest and is unconfirmed. Text gets visibly smaller in big jumps.
use_for: quickly bringing an oversized display headline down to fit a banner
roughing out a type hierarchy before fine-tuning sizes
avoid: exact sizes: type the value in the Character panel
small body text: a big step can overshoot, use Point Size Down
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("sizeStepDown") (inferred id); DOM: textRange.characterAttributes.size = <new size in pt> (unverified)

review.changes: removed the 5x / 10 pt / 2 pt step figures and the size -= 10 DOM call: none of those numbers is in the batch

cards.name: Font Size Step Up
cards.path: Edit/Keyboard Shortcuts.../Menu Commands/Other Text/Font Size Step Up
cards.summary: Enlarges the selected type by a bigger step than Point Size Up; Adobe's shortcut docs describe it as a multiple of the Size/Leading increment in Preferences > Type, but the step size is not in this harvest and is unconfirmed. Useful for fast, coarse scaling of display type.
use_for: blowing a poster or social-post headline up to display size quickly
testing how large a hero word can go before it breaks the layout
avoid: precise sizes or matching a spec: enter the size in the Character panel
scaling a whole lockup with mixed sizes proportionally: scale the object instead
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("sizeStepUp") (inferred id); DOM: textRange.characterAttributes.size = <new size in pt> (unverified)

review.changes: removed the 5x / 10 pt / 2 pt step figures and the size += 10 DOM call: none of those numbers is in the batch

cards.name: Highlight Font
cards.summary: Puts keyboard focus in the font family field (Character panel or Control/Properties panel) with the name highlighted, so you can type a new font name straight away. It changes no artwork by itself.
use_for: swapping fonts on a selected headline while trying options for a poster
keyboard-driven typesetting of labels and packaging copy
avoid: replacing one font across the whole document: use Type > Find/Replace Font
scripts: focusing a panel field does nothing useful, set textFont directly
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("highlightFont") only focuses the field (inferred id); same job in the DOM: textRange.characterAttributes.textFont = app.textFonts.getByName("<PostScript name>") (unverified)

review.changes: none

cards.name: Highlight Font (Secondary)
cards.summary: Second key binding for jumping to the font family field so a font name can be typed; by its name it does the same as Highlight Font. Its shortcut Alt+Shift+Ctrl+M is also the harvested shortcut of Type > Insert WhiteSpace Character > Thin Space, so while editing text the key may insert a thin space instead.
use_for: an alternative font-field shortcut for users who remap Alt+Shift+Ctrl+F
keyboard-driven font changes on selected text objects
avoid: using it with the cursor in text if you need a thin space (same keys)
document-wide font swaps: use Find/Replace Font
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("highlightFont2") only focuses the field (inferred id); DOM: textRange.characterAttributes.textFont = app.textFonts.getByName("<PostScript name>") (unverified)

review.changes: none (the Alt+Shift+Ctrl+M clash with Type > Insert WhiteSpace Character > Thin Space, ~thinSpace, text editing context, checked in the ai_menu harvest)

cards.name: Italic
cards.summary: Text-editing shortcut that italicises the selected characters, presumably by switching them to the Italic (or Oblique) style of their family since Illustrator has no faux italic; behaviour when the family lacks an italic is unverified. Works only while the cursor is in text.
use_for: setting a book or film title inside body copy
a quoted line or testimonial on a flyer
avoid: families with no italic style: pick a different family or a true italic instead of slanting with Shear
consistent styling across a long document: use a character style
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("~textItalic") (inferred id, text-editing context, likely needs a live text selection). DOM: set textRange.characterAttributes.textFont to the app.textFonts item whose .family is the current font's family and whose .style is its Italic style (unverified)

review.changes: DOM route no longer guesses a "<Family>-Italic" font name; it now picks the Italic style via TextFont.family / .style

cards.name: Justify All Lines
cards.path: Edit/Keyboard Shortcuts.../Menu Commands/Other Text/Justify All Lines
cards.summary: Force-justifies the selected paragraphs: every line, including the last one, is stretched to the full width of the text area, so a short last line gets wide gaps. Same as the Justify All Lines button in the Paragraph panel.
use_for: a single-line block that must span an exact width (masthead, spaced tagline)
boxy text blocks in a grid layout where the last line must also be flush
avoid: normal paragraphs: a short last line spreads into huge gaps, use Justify Text Left
point type: justification only shows on area type
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("justifyAll") (inferred id); DOM: textRange.paragraphAttributes.justification = Justification.FULLJUSTIFY (unverified)

review.changes: none

cards.name: Justify Text Center
cards.path: Edit/Keyboard Shortcuts.../Menu Commands/Other Text/Justify Text Center
cards.summary: Justifies the selected paragraphs with the last line centred: all full lines run flush to both edges and the final short line sits in the middle. Same as Justify with last line aligned center in the Paragraph panel; it has no default shortcut.
use_for: centred, justified intro text on a book cover or invitation
symmetrical text blocks under a centred headline
avoid: body text in columns: a centred last line looks odd, use Justify Text Left
narrow columns: justification opens rivers of white space
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("justifyCenter") (inferred id); DOM: textRange.paragraphAttributes.justification = Justification.FULLJUSTIFYLASTLINECENTER (unverified)

review.changes: none

cards.name: Justify Text Left
cards.path: Edit/Keyboard Shortcuts.../Menu Commands/Other Text/Justify Text Left
cards.summary: Justifies the selected paragraphs with the last line aligned left: full lines are flush to both edges, the last line stays ragged. This is the standard justified setting for body copy.
use_for: body copy in brochure and magazine-style columns
clean rectangular text blocks in annual reports and menus
avoid: narrow columns or large type: word gaps and rivers appear, use Left Align Text
headlines: use left, centre or Justify All Lines instead
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("justify") (inferred id); DOM: textRange.paragraphAttributes.justification = Justification.FULLJUSTIFYLASTLINELEFT (unverified)

review.changes: none

cards.name: Justify Text Right
cards.path: Edit/Keyboard Shortcuts.../Menu Commands/Other Text/Justify Text Right
cards.summary: Justifies the selected paragraphs with the last line aligned right: full lines run flush to both edges and the final line hugs the right edge. Matches Justify with last line aligned right in the Paragraph panel; no default shortcut.
use_for: justified text blocks placed against the right margin of a layout
justified sidebar or pull-quote blocks set against the right margin, where a flush-right last line echoes that edge
avoid: ordinary left-to-right body copy: readers expect the last line at the left, use Justify Text Left
narrow columns where justification causes rivers
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("justifyRight") (inferred id); DOM: textRange.paragraphAttributes.justification = Justification.FULLJUSTIFYLASTLINERIGHT (unverified)

review.changes: replaced the misleading 'right-to-left-reading feel' use_for

cards.name: Kern Looser
cards.summary: Text-editing shortcut that opens up the space: with the insertion point between two letters it adds kerning to that pair, and with a range selected it probably loosens tracking. The step per press is presumably the Tracking increment from Preferences > Type; not confirmed. Works only while editing text.
use_for: opening a tight letter pair in a logotype or headline
airing out all-caps titles a little at a time
avoid: setting an exact value: type it in the Character panel's kerning or tracking field
outside text editing: the same keys are Bring to Front for objects
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("~kernFurther") (inferred id, text-editing context). DOM: textRange.characters[i].kerning = <value in milli-ems> for one pair, or textRange.characterAttributes.tracking = <value in thousandths of an em> for a range (unverified)

review.changes: removed the invented += 20 step from the DOM route

cards.name: Kern Tighter
cards.summary: Text-editing shortcut that closes up the space: with the insertion point between two letters it removes kerning from that pair, and with a range selected it probably tightens tracking. The step is presumably the Tracking increment from Preferences > Type; not confirmed. Works only while editing text.
use_for: closing gaps in awkward pairs like AV, To, LT in a logo
tightening large display type that looks loose at size
avoid: small body text: tight spacing hurts legibility
outside text editing: the same keys are Send to Back for objects
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("~kernCloser") (inferred id, text-editing context). DOM: textRange.characters[i].kerning = <value in milli-ems> for one pair, or textRange.characterAttributes.tracking = <value in thousandths of an em> for a range (unverified)

review.changes: removed the invented -= 20 step from the DOM route

cards.name: Left Align Text
cards.path: Edit/Keyboard Shortcuts.../Menu Commands/Other Text/Left Align Text
cards.summary: Sets the selected paragraphs (or all text in selected type objects) to Align Left: lines start flush at the left edge and end ragged on the right. Same as the Align Left button in the Paragraph panel.
use_for: body copy and captions in most layouts
left-aligned editorial headlines and infographic labels
avoid: moving the text object itself to the left edge: use the Align panel
symmetrical layouts like invitations: use Center Text
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("leftAlign") (inferred id); DOM: textRange.paragraphAttributes.justification = Justification.LEFT (unverified)

review.changes: none

cards.name: Point Size Down
cards.path: Edit/Keyboard Shortcuts.../Menu Commands/Other Text/Point Size Down
cards.summary: Decreases the font size of the selected type by one Size/Leading increment, the value set in Preferences > Type. Small, controlled steps down.
use_for: nudging body copy smaller until it fits a text frame
fine-tuning caption and label sizes by eye
avoid: large reductions: use Font Size Step Down or type the size
scaling text and graphics together: scale the objects instead
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("faceSizeDown") (inferred id); DOM: textRange.characterAttributes.size -= <Size/Leading increment in pt> (unverified)

review.changes: removed the 2 pt default and the size -= 2 DOM call: the increment's value is not in the batch

cards.name: Point Size Up
cards.path: Edit/Keyboard Shortcuts.../Menu Commands/Other Text/Point Size Up
cards.summary: Increases the font size of the selected type by one Size/Leading increment, the value set in Preferences > Type. Small, controlled steps up.
use_for: bumping a subhead up until the hierarchy reads right
growing a line of text to fill a box by eye
avoid: big jumps: use Font Size Step Up or enter a size
matching an exact spec size: type it in the Character panel
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("faceSizeUp") (inferred id); DOM: textRange.characterAttributes.size += <Size/Leading increment in pt> (unverified)

review.changes: removed the 2 pt default and the size += 2 DOM call: the increment's value is not in the batch

cards.name: Right Align Text
cards.path: Edit/Keyboard Shortcuts.../Menu Commands/Other Text/Right Align Text
cards.summary: Sets the selected paragraphs to Align Right: lines end flush at the right edge and start ragged on the left. Same as the Align Right button in the Paragraph panel.
use_for: captions and labels that sit to the left of an image or rule
price columns, dates and sign-offs in menus and letterheads
avoid: long reading text: a ragged left edge is tiring, use Left Align Text
moving the object to the right edge: use the Align panel
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("rightAlign") (inferred id); DOM: textRange.paragraphAttributes.justification = Justification.RIGHT (unverified)

review.changes: none

cards.name: Spacing
cards.summary: Keyboard-only text command whose exact action was not confirmed; by its name and place it most likely opens the paragraph spacing (Justification) settings for the selected paragraphs: word spacing, letter spacing and glyph scaling. Treat as unverified until it is run.
use_for: controlling word and letter spacing in justified body copy to reduce rivers
allowing slight glyph scaling so justified columns set more evenly
avoid: changing spacing between two letters: use kerning, not paragraph spacing
relying on it in automation before its action is confirmed
cards.how: If it opens the Justification dialog: set Word Spacing, Letter Spacing and Glyph Scaling as Minimum / Desired / Maximum percentages, plus Auto Leading and Single Word Justification, then OK to apply to the selected paragraphs.
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("spacing") (inferred id, action unconfirmed); DOM: textRange.paragraphAttributes.desiredWordSpacing / minimumWordSpacing / maximumWordSpacing / desiredLetterSpacing / desiredGlyphScaling (unverified)

review.changes: none

cards.name: Subscript
cards.summary: Text-editing shortcut that sets the selected characters to subscript: smaller and dropped below the baseline, using the Subscript size and position from Document Setup's type options. Works only while editing text.
use_for: chemical formulas like H2O and CO2 on infographics
footnote-style indices and maths notation in diagrams
avoid: fonts with proper OpenType subscript/inferior figures: those are better drawn than the scaled synthetic version
objects selected with a selection tool: it is a text-editing command and only acts on characters selected inside a type object
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("~subscript") (inferred id, text-editing context). DOM: textRange.characterAttributes.baselinePosition = FontBaselineOption.SUBSCRIPT (unverified)

review.changes: reworded the unclear 'does nothing to unselected objects' avoid

cards.name: Superscript
cards.summary: Text-editing shortcut that sets the selected characters to superscript: smaller and raised above the baseline, using the Superscript size and position from Document Setup's type options. Works only while editing text.
use_for: trademark and registered marks, ordinals (1st, 2nd) and footnote markers
units like m2 and exponents on infographics and spec sheets
avoid: fonts with OpenType superior figures or ordinals: use those for better-drawn glyphs
raising text by a custom amount: use Baseline Shift in the Character panel
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("~superScript") (inferred id, text-editing context). DOM: textRange.characterAttributes.baselinePosition = FontBaselineOption.SUPERSCRIPT (unverified)

review.changes: none

cards.name: Toggle Auto Hyphenation
cards.path: Edit/Keyboard Shortcuts.../Menu Commands/Other Text/Toggle Auto Hyphenation
cards.summary: Turns automatic hyphenation on or off for the selected paragraphs (the Hyphenate checkbox in the Paragraph panel). With it on, long words break across lines with a hyphen, which evens out justified and ragged text.
use_for: smoothing word gaps in justified brochure columns
switching hyphenation off in headlines and logos where broken words look wrong
avoid: fixing one bad break: insert a discretionary hyphen or adjust that line instead
brand names and URLs: switch hyphenation off for those paragraphs
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("toggleAutoHyphen") (inferred id); DOM: textRange.paragraphAttributes.hyphenation = true / false (unverified)

review.changes: none (CDR Text/Use Hyphenation checked: exists, same job)

cards.name: Toggle Line Composer
cards.path: Edit/Keyboard Shortcuts.../Menu Commands/Other Text/Toggle Line Composer
cards.summary: Switches the selected paragraphs between the Adobe Every-line Composer (the default, which balances breaks over the whole paragraph) and the Single-line Composer (which breaks each line on its own). Line breaks and spacing can shift when you toggle.
use_for: keeping manual line breaks stable while hand-tuning a headline (single-line)
getting more even spacing in justified body copy (every-line)
avoid: fixing a single bad line break: insert a forced line break or adjust tracking
finished layouts: toggling can reflow text and push lines into overset
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("toggleLineComposer") (inferred id); DOM: textRange.paragraphAttributes.everyLineComposer = true / false (unverified)

review.changes: none

cards.name: Tracking
cards.summary: Puts keyboard focus in the tracking field of the Character panel (Adobe's shortcut list calls Alt+Ctrl+K highlight kerning, so it may be the kerning field) so a value can be typed. It changes no artwork by itself.
use_for: typing an exact tracking value for spaced-out caps in a logo or title
keyboard-driven letter-spacing adjustments on headlines
avoid: small nudges while editing text: Kern Looser / Kern Tighter (Shift+Ctrl+] / Shift+Ctrl+[) step the spacing without a panel
scripts: focusing the field does nothing, set tracking in the DOM
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("tracking") only focuses the panel field (inferred id); same job in the DOM: textRange.characterAttributes.tracking = <1/1000 em> (unverified)

review.changes: replaced the unharvested Alt+Left/Right arrow shortcut with the batch's Kern Looser / Kern Tighter keys

cards.name: Underline
cards.summary: Text-editing shortcut that underlines the selected characters, the same as the Underline button in the Character panel; the line follows the text and takes its fill colour. Works only while editing text.
use_for: marking a link or call to action in a web banner mock-up
emphasis in forms, labels and annotated diagrams
avoid: a decorative underline with custom weight, offset or colour: draw a line or use an Appearance stroke
headline emphasis in print design: weight or colour usually reads better
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("~textUnderline") (inferred id, text-editing context). DOM: textRange.characterAttributes.underline = true (unverified)

review.changes: none

cards.name: Uniform Type
cards.summary: Resets the character scaling of the selected type to 100%, removing squashed or stretched letterforms; Adobe's shortcut list names it reset horizontal scale, and whether vertical scale is reset too is unverified. The font's true proportions come back.
use_for: undoing distorted type in a file inherited from someone else
restoring proper letter shapes before final logo or packaging artwork
avoid: type that was scaled as an object (bounding-box scaling) rather than by character scale: scale the object back instead
condensed looks you want: choose a real condensed font rather than horizontal scaling
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("clearTypeScale") (inferred id); DOM: textRange.characterAttributes.horizontalScale = 100, plus verticalScale = 100 if the command proves to reset both (unverified)

review.changes: DOM route no longer asserts vertical scale is reset, matching the summary's open point
